scenes.heading: Enlargements and similar figures
scenes.say: Zooming a photo, printing a poster and building a model car all use enlargements. In this video you will enlarge shapes from a centre, find scale factors, and use them to work out missing lengths in similar figures.

scenes.heading: Think of it like this
scenes.everyday: Pinch-to-zoom makes every part of a photo grow evenly
scenes.science: An enlargement multiplies every length by the same scale factor k
scenes.breaks: Zooming crops parts off the screen; an enlargement keeps the whole shape.
scenes.say: When you pinch to zoom on a photo, everything grows evenly. A face two centimetres wide becomes four, and the nose doubles too, so nothing looks stretched. That even growth is an enlargement. The difference is that zooming crops parts off the screen, but an enlargement keeps the whole shape.

scenes.heading: Enlarging from a centre
notes: Rays start at the centre O
Each distance from O is doubled
scenes.say: First the small triangle, then dashed rays from the centre O through each corner. Each image point is twice as far from O as the original, because the scale factor is two. So A at one, one moves to A dash at two, two, and every side doubles.
scenes.caption: Dashed rays go from the centre O through each corner. Each image point is twice as far from O, because k = 2. A(1, 1) moves to A′(2, 2), and every side doubles.

scenes.heading: The scale factor
scenes.say: The scale factor k is the new length divided by the old length, using one pair of matching sides. If k is more than one, the shape gets bigger; between zero and one, it gets smaller. Areas are multiplied by k squared.
scenes.caption: k = new length ÷ old length. If k is more than 1 the shape gets bigger; between 0 and 1 it gets smaller. Areas are multiplied by k².

scenes.heading: Similar trapezia
scenes.say: Here are two similar trapezia. Nine divided by six is one point five, and every other side is also one point five times as long: four becomes six, three becomes four point five, five becomes seven point five. The right angles stay right angles.
scenes.caption: 9 ÷ 6 = 1.5, and every other side is also 1.5 times as long: 4 → 6, 3 → 4.5, 5 → 7.5. The right angles stay right angles.

scenes.heading: Worked example
scenes.question: Enlarge P(2, 3) from centre C(1, 1) by scale factor 3.
lines: From C to P: 1 right, 2 up
scenes.say: Enlarge P at two, three from centre C at one, one by scale factor three. From C to P is one right and two up. Times three gives three right and six up. Add that back on to C: P dash is at four, seven.
scenes.caption: From C to P is 1 right and 2 up. Times 3 gives 3 right and 6 up. Add that back on to C: P′ = (4, 7).

points: Similar: equal angles, sides in one ratio
scenes.say: Quick recap. An enlargement needs a centre and a scale factor. The scale factor is new divided by old. Angles never change. Similar figures have equal angles and all sides in the same ratio. Lengths multiply by k, areas by k squared. Now try the practice questions!
scenes.caption: An enlargement needs a centre and a scale factor. k = new ÷ old. Angles never change. Similar figures have equal angles and all sides in the same ratio. Lengths × k, areas × k². Now try the practice questions!
